system_profile.system_purpose: MyBatis 3 (org.mybatis:mybatis v3.6.0) is a Java persistence and SQL mapper framework that couples domain objects (POJOs, Java Records, Maps, and Collections) with SQL statements or stored procedures via XML descriptors or Java annotations, providing dynamic SQL generation, L1/L2 caching, JDK dynamic proxy mappers, bidirectional TypeHandler conversions, and pluggable JDBC execution.
system_profile.domain_context: Relational database data-mapper persistence layer for Java SE and Jakarta EE / Spring enterprise applications, operating directly atop standard JDBC (java.sql / javax.sql) without full ORM entity-state tracking overhead.
tech_stack: JDBC (java.sql / javax.sql DataSource, Connection, PreparedStatement, CallableStatement, ResultSet)
OGNL 3.4.16 (shaded into org.apache.ibatis.ognl for Dynamic SQL expression evaluation)
Javassist 3.33.0-GA (shaded into org.apache.ibatis.javassist for lazy-loading bytecode proxies)
JAXP DOM / XPath (javax.xml.xpath / org.w3c.dom for XML configuration and mapper DTD/XSD parsing)
JUnit Jupiter 6.1.3, Mockito 5.24.0, AssertJ 3.27.7, HSQLDB 2.7.4, Apache Derby 10.17.1.0, H2 2.5.252, Testcontainers 1.21.4 (test suite)
external_integrations: JDBC Drivers & Relational Databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server, HSQLDB, H2, Apache Derby)
JNDI Naming Contexts (JndiDataSourceFactory) and External Connection Pools (HikariCP, Agroal, DBCP)
Pluggable Logging Frameworks (SLF4J 2.0, Apache Log4j 2.26, Reload4j, Apache Commons Logging, JDK java.util.logging, StdOut)

structure_map.boundary_assessment: MyBatis 3's 20 packages under org.apache.ibatis.* follow a clear 3-tier hierarchy (Session/Binding/Annotations -> Builder/Mapping/Scripting/Executor/Plugin -> Reflection/Type/Cache/Transaction/DataSource/Parsing/IO/Logging). Foundation packages (cache, plugin, parsing, logging, exceptions) are strictly acyclic, while a hub-and-spoke coupling exists around org.apache.ibatis.session.Configuration and UnknownTypeHandler.

execution_flows.name: Configuration & Mapper Compilation Flow (Bootstrap Phase)
steps: SqlSessionFactoryBuilder instantiates XMLConfigBuilder with an XPathParser and parses <configuration> root sections (<properties>, <settings>, <typeAliases>, <plugins>, <objectFactory>, <environments>, <typeHandlers>, <mappers>).
For XML mappers, XMLMapperBuilder parses <cache>, <resultMap>, <sql>, and delegates statement tags (<select>, <insert>, <update>, <delete>) to XMLStatementBuilder.

For interface mappers, MapperRegistry registers a MapperProxyFactory<T> and invokes MapperAnnotationBuilder.parse() to compile @Select/@Insert/@Update/@Delete/@SelectProvider and @Results/@Result annotations.

LanguageDriver (XMLLanguageDriver) compiles SQL text and dynamic tags (<if>, <where>, <foreach>) into DynamicSqlSource or RawSqlSource, and MapperBuilderAssistant registers immutable MappedStatement and ResultMap objects in Configuration.

execution_flows.name: Mapper Proxy Query & L1/L2 Cache Execution Pipeline
execution_flows.trigger: Application calls a method on a Mapper interface obtained via SqlSession.getMapper(Class<T>)
steps: MapperProxyFactory creates a JDK Proxy backed by MapperProxy, which caches a MapperMethodInvoker (PlainMethodInvoker wrapping MapperMethod or DefaultMethodInvoker for Java 8+ default methods).

MapperMethod.execute(SqlSession, Object[]) resolves the SQL command type (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/FLUSH), converts arguments via ParamNameResolver into a ParamMap or single param, and calls DefaultSqlSession.selectList/selectOne/update.

DefaultSqlSession looks up the MappedStatement in Configuration and delegates to Executor (CachingExecutor wrapping SimpleExecutor/ReuseExecutor/BatchExecutor, decorated by InterceptorChain.pluginAll).

CachingExecutor computes a CacheKey from MappedStatement ID, RowBounds, BoundSql SQL string, and parameter values; checks Namespace L2 TransactionalCache, then delegates to BaseExecutor L1 PerpetualCache.

On cache miss, SimpleExecutor obtains a JDBC Connection from Transaction, creates a RoutingStatementHandler -> PreparedStatementHandler, binds parameters via DefaultParameterHandler and TypeHandlers, executes PreparedStatement, and delegates ResultSet mapping to DefaultResultSetHandler.

execution_flows.name: ResultSet Mapping, Nested Associations & Reflective Hydration Flow
execution_flows.trigger: DefaultResultSetHandler.handleResultSets(Statement) processes JDBC ResultSet rows after statement execution
steps: DefaultResultSetHandler wraps the JDBC ResultSet in a ResultSetWrapper (caching column names, JDBC types, and TypeHandlers) and resolves the root ResultMap (and Discriminator if configured).

For simple ResultMaps, createResultObject instantiates the target JavaBean, Record, or primitive via ObjectFactory or constructor mappings (ResultMappingConstructorResolver), then applies automatic and explicit property mappings via MetaObject -> BeanWrapper -> Reflector.
For nested ResultMaps (<association> / <collection> joins), handleRowValuesForNestedResultMap computes compound CacheKeys to deduplicate parent objects and merges child rows into parent collections.

For nested select queries with lazyLoadingEnabled, ResultLoaderMap and ProxyFactory (JavassistProxyFactory) wrap the target bean in a bytecode proxy that defers child query execution until getter invocation.

state_and_storage: Configuration singleton (application-scoped): Thread-safe after bootstrap; stores ConcurrentHashMap/StrictMap registries of MappedStatements, ResultMaps, ParameterMaps, Caches, KeyGenerators, TypeHandlers, TypeAliases, and MapperRegistry.

L2 Cache (Namespace-scoped): Shared across SqlSessions via CachingExecutor and TransactionalCacheManager; uncommitted entries are buffered per transaction in TransactionalCache and flushed to decorated PerpetualCache (LruCache, SerializedCache, SynchronizedCache) only upon SqlSession.commit().

L1 Local Cache (SqlSession-scoped): Non-thread-safe PerpetualCache inside BaseExecutor storing query results and deferred loads for the lifetime of a single SqlSession or statement (LocalCacheScope.SESSION vs STATEMENT), cleared on any insert/update/delete/commit/rollback.

ThreadLocal ErrorContext: Per-thread diagnostic breadcrumbs (ErrorContext.instance()) recording the active XML resource, MappedStatement ID, SQL string, and activity cause prior to throwing PersistenceException.
execution_flow_map.error_and_concurrency_model: All checked JDBC SQLExceptions and reflective exceptions are translated via ExceptionFactory.wrapException into unchecked PersistenceException subclasses (ExecutorException, BindingException, BuilderException, ScriptingException, TypeException, ReflectionException) enriched with ThreadLocal ErrorContext state. Concurrency follows a strict two-tier contract: SqlSessionFactory and Configuration are application-scoped and thread-safe at runtime (backed by ConcurrentHashMap in DefaultReflectorFactory, OgnlCache, and MapperProxy), whereas SqlSession, Executor, and DefaultResultSetHandler are strictly request/transaction-scoped and confined to a single thread.

audit_dimensions.title: Interpret Java AST Facts & Evaluate Quality/Generics/Imports/Security
audit_dimensions.summary: MyBatis 3.6.0 demonstrates 100.0% import hygiene (0 wildcard or unsorted imports across 393 source files and 23,364 LOC) and 99.9% generic type coverage across 2,721 methods. As a reflection-driven SQL mapper, untyped Object parameters/returns and @SuppressWarnings("unchecked") are concentrated in dynamic proxy dispatchers (MapperMethod, MapperProxyFactory), OGNL expression bridges, and TypeHandler registries. Key structural observations include 59 high-complexity methods led by DefaultParameterHandler.setParameters (cognitive=129) and PooledDataSource.popConnection (cognitive=78), 17 builder methods with >6 parameters in MapperBuilderAssistant, 22 class-level dependency cycles (primarily Configuration <-> MapperRegistry <-> MapperAnnotationBuilder <-> UnknownTypeHandler and package-internal reflection/VFS pairs), and 16.3% Javadoc coverage. Deserialization in AbstractSerialStateHolder.readResolve is guarded by SerialFilterChecker.check() encouraging JEP-290 jdk.serialFilter.

audit_dimensions.title: Evaluate Public API Boundaries, Import Purity, SemVer & Diátaxis Docs
audit_dimensions.summary: MyBatis 3.6.0 exemplifies Java library packaging hygiene: it declares Automatic-Module-Name 'org.mybatis' and explicit OSGi exports (pom.xml:86-91), ships package-info.java across all 20 packages, imposes zero mandatory transitive runtime dependencies by marking all third-party bridges <optional>true</optional> and shading OGNL/Javassist into org.apache.ibatis.*, never calls System.exit(), and routes all logging through its pluggable LogFactory SPI (where StdOutImpl is strictly an opt-in adapter). Improvement opportunities center on expanding inline Javadoc coverage (currently 16.3% with 24 @param mismatches) and reducing 19-22 parameter overloads in MapperBuilderAssistant.

audit_dimensions.title: Evaluate Supply-Chain CVEs, Container Misconfigs, Secrets, Dangerous Sinks & API Boundaries
audit_dimensions.summary: MyBatis 3.6.0 demonstrates a strong security and supply-chain posture for a foundational Java persistence library. Trivy SCA (v0.69.3) against pom.xml and dependencies-lock.json reported zero CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW CVEs across all 9 direct and transitive dependencies (including shaded ognl 3.4.16 and javassist 3.33.0-GA) and zero container misconfigurations or leaked secrets. XML parsing in XPathParser enforces XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING=true, expandEntityReferences=false, and offline DTD resolution via XMLMapperEntityResolver. The single CWE-502 ObjectInputStream sink in AbstractSerialStateHolder.java:110 (and SerializedCache.java:102) is guarded by SerialFilterChecker.check(), which inspects JEP-290 jdk.serialFilter and logs a warning if unconfigured, though it defaults to warn-only rather than enforcing a per-stream ObjectInputFilter whitelist. Supply-chain governance includes a committed dependencies-lock.json and Maven Wrapper (mvnw), with minor gaps in repository-local SECURITY.md and automated Dependabot/Renovate configuration.

audit_dimensions.title: Evaluate Maven/Gradle Build, Supply Chain & Dependencies
audit_dimensions.summary: MyBatis 3.6.0 exhibits disciplined Maven packaging and dependency management: all 9 non-test dependencies in pom.xml are pinned to exact versions and marked <optional>true</optional> or <scope>provided</scope>, test frameworks (JUnit Jupiter 6.1.3, Mockito 5.24.0, AssertJ 3.27.7, HSQLDB 2.7.4, Derby 10.17.1.0, H2 2.5.252, Testcontainers 1.21.4) are isolated under <scope>test</scope>, and maven-shade-plugin relocates ognl and javassist under org.apache.ibatis.* to eliminate classpath shadowing. Reproducibility is enforced via mvnw, dependencies-lock.json, and project.build.outputTimestamp. Minor improvement opportunities exist around baseline Java 11 bytecode targeting (pom.xml:67-68) and adding a standalone SECURITY.md policy.

audit_dimensions.title: Evaluate JUnit Test Suite Completeness & Structure
audit_dimensions.summary: MyBatis 3.6.0 maintains a comprehensive, well-structured JUnit Jupiter 6.1.3 test suite comprising 372 test files and 1,918 test methods (nearly 1:1 with the 393 source files, achieving 81.5% direct module-name mirror coverage plus an extensive src/test/java/org/apache/ibatis/submitted/ regression suite covering 300+ historical GitHub/Jira issues). In-memory relational databases (HSQLDB 2.7.4, Apache Derby 10.17.1.0, H2 2.5.252) seeded via BaseDataTest.runScript provide deterministic offline SQL execution, while external DB tests are cleanly isolated via @Tag("TestcontainersTests"). Of the 126 methods flagged by static AST as lacking standard assert*/verify calls, inspection of BindingTest.java (lines 151-184) and XmlConfigBuilderTest.java (lines 271-290) confirms they perform BDD exception assertions via com.googlecode.catchexception.apis.BDDCatchException.when(...)/then(caughtException()).

strengths: Zero mandatory runtime transitive dependencies: all logging bridges (SLF4J, Log4j2, Reload4j, Commons Logging) and bytecode/expression libraries (OGNL, Javassist, CGLIB) are declared <optional>true</optional> in pom.xml (lines 115-134, 287-310).

Conflict-free fat-jar shading: maven-shade-plugin (pom.xml:365-411) relocates ognl to org.apache.ibatis.ognl and javassist to org.apache.ibatis.javassist so downstream applications never suffer version collisions.
Reproducible build configuration with committed Maven Wrapper (mvnw), dependencies-lock.json, and deterministic project.build.outputTimestamp (pom.xml:100).
100.0% import hygiene across all 393 Java source files with zero wildcard imports (import foo.*) enforced by Maven formatting rules.
99.9% generic type safety coverage across 2,721 methods, with strong typing throughout TypeHandler<T>, Cursor<T>, and Builder APIs.
Proactive JEP-290 deserialization defense in SerialFilterChecker.java and AbstractSerialStateHolder.java (lines 107-110).

Zero transitive dependency pollution for library consumers: all 9 compile/provided dependencies are optional, and OGNL + Javassist are shaded into org.apache.ibatis.ognl and org.apache.ibatis.javassist (pom.xml:397-406).
Clean library runtime behavior: zero System.exit() calls, zero import-time network I/O, and pluggable LogFactory abstraction supporting SLF4J, Log4j2, Reload4j, Commons Logging, JUL, and NoLogging.
Complete package-info.java coverage across all 20 packages under src/main/java/org/apache/ibatis/.
Near 1:1 test-to-source file ratio (372 test files for 393 source files) with 1,918 JUnit 5 test methods and 81.5% direct module mirror coverage.
Hermetic in-memory relational testing via BaseDataTest (HSQLDB, Apache Derby, H2) requiring zero external network services for standard unit/integration test runs.
Dedicated regression suite under src/test/java/org/apache/ibatis/submitted/ isolating reproductions for hundreds of real-world SQL mapping, caching, and concurrency edge cases.
100% offline test execution success: 1,990 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors (19 skipped) out of 2,009 JUnit 5 tests running with --network=none against embedded HSQLDB, Apache Derby, and H2.
High measured JaCoCo coverage: 87.4% line coverage (9,985 / 11,418 statements) and 82.7% branch coverage across all 20 packages.
Clean separation of JDK 16+ illegal-access legacy tests via @Tag('RequireIllegalAccess') and external DB container tests via @Tag('TestcontainersTests') in pom.xml:83.

Zero CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW vulnerabilities in Trivy 0.69.3 SCA across all Maven dependencies (ognl:3.4.16, javassist:3.33.0-GA, slf4j-api:2.0.20, log4j-api:2.26.1, reload4j:1.2.27, mssql-jdbc:13.6.1.jre11).

Hardened XML configuration and mapper parsing in XPathParser.java:233-243 using XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING=true, setExpandEntityReferences(false), and offline classpath DTD resolution via XMLMapperEntityResolver.
Proactive JEP-290 deserialization filter awareness via SerialFilterChecker.check() invoked prior to ObjectInputStream reads in AbstractSerialStateHolder.java:107 and SerializedCache.java:100.
Deterministic supply-chain reproducibility via committed dependencies-lock.json and Maven Wrapper (mvnw) with zero hardcoded secrets or credential artifacts.

findings.description: PooledDataSource.popConnection has cognitive complexity 78 and 117 lines mixing idle pool checkout, active connection eviction on maxCheckoutTime, bad connection retry loops, and PoolState metrics.
findings.recommendation: Decompose popConnection into smaller private methods handling idle connection retrieval, overdue active connection reclamation, and connection validation.

findings.description: DefaultParameterHandler.setParameters exhibits cognitive complexity 129 due to deeply nested parameter value extraction, ParamMap generic type resolution, MetaClass lookup, and null TypeHandler fallback branches.
findings.recommendation: Extract helper methods for parameter value resolution (resolveParameterValue), ParamMap generic type inference (resolveParamMapGenericType), and TypeHandler selection (resolveTypeHandler).

findings.evidence: SerialFilterChecker.check(); try (ObjectInputStream in = new ObjectInputStream(new ByteArrayInputStream(this.userBeanBytes))) { this.userBean = in.readObject(); ... }
findings.description: AbstractSerialStateHolder.readResolve() deserializes lazy-loading proxy state via ObjectInputStream (CWE-502). While SerialFilterChecker.check() checks for a JVM-wide JEP-290 jdk.serialFilter, it only logs a one-time warning when no filter is configured instead of attaching a restrictive per-stream ObjectInputFilter or failing closed.
findings.recommendation: Allow configuring a dedicated ObjectInputFilter on Configuration (or enforce a default package allowlist on the ObjectInputStream instance via in.setObjectInputFilter(...)) when jdk.serialFilter is not set at the JVM level.

findings.evidence: Circular dependency: Arg -> UnknownTypeHandler -> Configuration -> MapperRegistry -> MapperAnnotationBuilder -> Arg
findings.description: @Arg and @Case annotations reference the concrete implementation class UnknownTypeHandler.class as their default typeHandler attribute, creating a compile-time cycle from annotations into type, session, binding, and builder.
findings.recommendation: Decouple annotation defaults by referencing the TypeHandler.class interface as the default sentinel or breaking UnknownTypeHandler's direct dependency on Configuration.

findings.recommendation: Update @param tags in AbstractSQL.java, ResolverUtil.java, and MapperBuilderAssistant.java to match exact method parameter identifiers.

findings.description: Maven compiler target defaults to Java 11 (pom.xml:67-68) for broad legacy compatibility, though JDK 17+ and 19+ activation profiles are defined at lines 471-488.
findings.recommendation: Consider advancing the baseline bytecode target to Java 17 or Java 21 LTS in future major releases to leverage modern JVM intrinsics, records, and sealed types natively.

findings.evidence: if (firstInvocation && SERIAL_FILTER_MISSING) { firstInvocation = false; log.warn("As you are using functionality that deserializes object streams, it is recommended to define the JEP-290 serial filter..."); }
findings.description: SerialFilterChecker.check() uses a non-volatile static boolean firstInvocation and emits a single warning log when jdk.serialFilter is missing, permitting subsequent ObjectInputStream deserializations in SerializedCache and AbstractSerialStateHolder to proceed unfiltered.
findings.recommendation: Provide a strict mode configuration flag (e.g., strictSerialFilter=true) that throws a PersistenceException or SerializedCacheException if deserialization is attempted without an active JEP-290 ObjectInputFilter.

findings.evidence: 126 test methods use BDDCatchException.when(() -> ...); then(caughtException()).isInstanceOf(...) instead of JUnit 5 Assertions.assertThrows or AssertJ assertThatThrownBy
findings.description: 126 test methods across BindingTest.java (lines 151, 169, 548) and XmlConfigBuilderTest.java (lines 271, 284) rely on the third-party catch-exception library (which requires byte-buddy-agent and --add-opens java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED in pom.xml:97) rather than standard JUnit 5 / AssertJ exception assertions.
findings.recommendation: Migrate remaining BDDCatchException.when/then(caughtException()) usages to AssertJ Assertions.assertThatThrownBy(...) or JUnit 5 Assertions.assertThrows(...) so the catch-exception dependency can be retired.

action_plan.title: Decompose high-complexity hot paths in DefaultParameterHandler and PooledDataSource
action_plan.action: Extract focused private helper methods in DefaultParameterHandler.setParameters (cognitive=129), PooledDataSource.popConnection (cognitive=78), and MapperAnnotationBuilder.getReturnType (cognitive=68) to bring per-method cognitive complexity below 25.
action_plan.expected_impact: Improves readability, unit testability, and maintainability of parameter binding and connection pooling hot paths.

action_plan.title: Add Optional Strict Per-Stream ObjectInputFilter Enforcement for Deserialization
action_plan.action: Support configuring a custom ObjectInputFilter (Java 9+) or fail-closed strict mode in SerialFilterChecker so applications using SerializedCache or lazy-loader serialization are protected even when the global JVM jdk.serialFilter property is omitted.
action_plan.expected_impact: Eliminates CWE-502 unsafe deserialization exposure when L2 cache or lazy state payloads are stored in external or shared media.

action_plan.title: Fix Javadoc @param mismatches and break @Arg -> UnknownTypeHandler cycle
action_plan.action: Synchronize the 24 mismatched Javadoc @param tags in AbstractSQL, ResolverUtil, and MapperBuilderAssistant, and decouple @Arg/@Case from concrete UnknownTypeHandler -> Configuration dependencies.
action_plan.expected_impact: Eliminates Javadoc compiler warnings and removes the 4 cross-package dependency cycles.

action_plan.title: Plan baseline JDK target migration from Java 11 to Java 17/21 LTS
action_plan.action: Update <java.version> and <java.release.version> in pom.xml (lines 67-68) to 17 or 21 LTS on the next major release line and consolidate legacy JDK activation profiles.
action_plan.expected_impact: Enables native Java records, pattern matching, and modern bytecode optimizations without multi-profile workarounds.

action_plan.title: Publish SECURITY.md Emphasizing #{} Parameter Binding and JEP-290 Serial Filters
action_plan.action: Add a SECURITY.md policy detailing upstream security reporting channels, mandatory JEP-290 jdk.serialFilter patterns for SerializedCache, and safe #{} PreparedStatement parameter binding versus ${} OGNL string interpolation.
action_plan.expected_impact: Improves OpenSSF Scorecard supply-chain governance and helps downstream developers prevent SQL injection and deserialization misconfigurations.

action_plan.title: Add SECURITY.md disclosure policy and dependency update config
action_plan.action: Add a SECURITY.md file detailing upstream MyBatis security reporting procedures and commit renovate.json for automated dependency monitoring.
action_plan.expected_impact: Improves OpenSSF Scorecard supply-chain governance posture.

action_plan.title: Add unit tests for non-LocationAware logger wrapper fallbacks
action_plan.action: Add unit tests in src/test/java/org/apache/ibatis/logging/ exercising Slf4jLoggerImpl and Log4j2LoggerImpl directly with mock Logger instances.
action_plan.expected_impact: Eliminates 0% coverage gaps in fallback logging adapters.

action_plan.title: Migrate remaining catch-exception tests to AssertJ assertThatThrownBy or JUnit 5 assertThrows
action_plan.action: Replace BDDCatchException.when(...)/then(caughtException()) calls in 126 test methods with AssertJ assertThatThrownBy(...) and remove com.github.hazendaz.catch-exception from pom.xml.
action_plan.expected_impact: Simplifies the test dependency graph and eliminates bytecode agent overhead for exception assertions.

summary: MyBatis 3 (v3.6.0) achieves an overall PNI501 engineering score of 90/100 (Grade S). Across 393 Java source files (23,364 LOC) and 372 JUnit 5 test files, the codebase exhibits 100.0% import hygiene, 99.9% generic type coverage, zero mandatory runtime dependencies (with OGNL 3.4.16 and Javassist 3.33.0-GA shaded into org.apache.ibatis.*), zero Trivy dependency CVEs, and 100% offline test reliability (1,990 passed, 0 failed) with 87.4% measured JaCoCo line coverage and 82.7% branch coverage. Key areas for engineering refinement include decomposing high-complexity methods in DefaultParameterHandler (cognitive=129) and PooledDataSource (cognitive=78), decoupling @Arg/@Case from UnknownTypeHandler to eliminate cross-package compile cycles, offering a strict per-stream ObjectInputFilter mode in SerialFilterChecker, and synchronizing Javadoc @param tags.
